papers.title: Bounds on polynomial approximations of the discrete logarithm function
papers.authors: Swastik Kopparty, Rishabh Kothary, Ashutosh Shankar
papers.summary: Improves Coppersmith–Shparlinski: any f in F_p[X] of degree <= D agrees with dlog on at most (1+o(1))sqrt(Dp) points (Johnson bound of RS list decoding; proof builds many 'conjugate' approximants from one via the almost-homomorphism dlog(x)+dlog(y) in dlog(xy)+{0,-1} plus Szemeredi), O(p^{2/5}) for D=1 via Bourgain extractor + Lewko/Miao–Xie incidence bounds; bivariate Q(x,dlog x)=0 vanishing bounded by (1+o(1))D sqrt(p). Conjecture 1.1: true bound ~ D log p/log(D+1). PDF intro read; multiplicative group F_p^* only, no elliptic-curve statement.
papers.relevance: Direct negative-result template for lever 8 (x-functional filters, KN-OPEN-91d4f6) and for coordinate-statistic hunts: any algebraic functional of low degree correlated with the logarithm is bounded by a Johnson-type agreement bound. The EC analogue (polynomials in x(P) agreeing with log_G(P), or Q(x(P),log P)=0; cf. Lange–Winterhof) is not treated here and is the natural question for the programme.
papers.suggested_route: Formulate the EC analogue: for toy E/F_p (20–30 bits) compute max agreement of degree-<=D polynomials in x(P) with log_G(P) via linear algebra over sampled points; compare to sqrt(D r). Prove the analogue using the same conjugate trick (the EC log is an exact homomorphism, so the 'almost' complication vanishes) — this would be a theorem closing linear/low-degree x-functional filters, not an attack. Classification: accounting/obstruction.

papers.title: Deterministic Root-Finding over Finite Fields with Elliptic Curves
papers.summary: Deterministic root finding of split f in F_q[X] using an auxiliary elliptic curve E and its twist with smooth group orders (elliptic preprocessing datum D; Xi(D)=largest prime of |E||E~|). Roots are encoded injectively into E(F_q) u E~(F_q) ('lifting split polynomials to split divisors'), then an 'elliptic Mignotte–Schnorr recursion' decomposes split divisors deterministically along the smooth group structure; online cost O~(Xi^2 n log^2 q + n^omega log q + n log^3 q), unconditional. Conjecture 1.5: Hasse interval contains U with q+1-U and q+1+U both (log q)^c-smooth. Magma prototype handles p > 2^63. Section 8 asks about more general curves and other algebraic groups. Mentions an unreviewed OpenAI preprint claiming unconditional deterministic factoring.
papers.relevance: Lever 2 (root finding beyond two summands) is about root-finding structure for S_4 membership; this paper is the mirror image: it uses an elliptic curve's group law as the root-finding engine for arbitrary polynomials over F_q. For the programme the relevant object is 'deterministic decomposition of split divisors on elliptic curves' (Sec. 5.2): a divisor on E whose points are unknown is decomposed using only group structure of a smooth-order auxiliary curve. Because the auxiliary curve is chosen, not the target, no ECDLP leverage is expected (the target r is prime); but it is a new representation-dependent map F_q -> E(F_q) u E~(F_q) that is injective and deterministic, which touches the 'only door' (field representation of coordinates).
papers.suggested_route: Toy experiment: implement the encoding x -> point on E or E~ (PARI) for a smooth-order auxiliary curve over F_p (p ~ 2^20–2^30); test whether the summation-polynomial root-finding step of a prime-field S_3/S_4 oracle is faster than Cantor–Zassenhaus/msolve root isolation — if it is, it is engineering (constant factor). Also check Sec. 8.3 'other algebraic groups' for whether the roles can be swapped (target curve as the group whose split divisors are decomposed) — expected answer: requires smooth order, so killed by prime r (name the obstruction: Mignotte–Schnorr recursion needs smooth group order).

papers.title: Hamming Ideals and Gröbner Bases for ISD-like Syndrome Decoding
papers.authors: Roberto La Scala, Marco Marchesin, Sharwan K. Tiwari
papers.summary: Systematic algebra of the Hamming variety H_t = {v in F_2^n : wt(v)=t}: by Lucas' theorem the Hamming ideal is <e_{2^k} - t_k> + field equations (binary digits of the weight are elementary symmetric functions of degree 2^k). Convolution identities and Lucas factorizations give equivalent 'Convolution', 'Factorized Convolution' and 'Quadratic Factorized Convolution' Hamming ideals with auxiliary variables and generators of degree <= 2 (Prop. 5.3). GBDecode fixes only part of an information set and solves the rest by Gröbner bases via MultiSolve (exhaustive partial assignment + many small GBs). Experiments at Classic McEliece Category-1 sizes. PDF intro and Sections 2–5 read.
papers.relevance: KN-OPEN-5e3dd0 (lever 6): a Hamming-ball factor base over F_{2^n} at prime n has a bounded-degree membership ideal. This paper gives the explicit quadratic model with O(n log n) auxiliary variables, which is exactly the ingredient needed to adjoin Hamming-weight membership to a Weil-descended S_{m+1} system without raising the degree of the input system. It does not touch elliptic curves.
papers.suggested_route: Experiment for LEAD-ICB-nonlinear-frob-stable-bases: at n=13..25, m=2,3, replace the F_2-subspace base by a Hamming ball of radius w in a normal basis (Frobenius-stable by construction since Frobenius permutes coordinates in a normal basis), adjoin the Quadratic Factorized Convolution Hamming ideal, and measure msolve solving degree and time versus the subspace base of equal size; falsifier: solving degree grows with n faster than for subspace bases, or coverage is no better. Also measure whether the Frobenius action gives the usual /n relation saving.

papers.title: Symmetric Models for Syndrome Decoding
papers.date: 2026-09-12 (3 days before window; included as borderline)
papers.summary: Polynomial model of exact binary syndrome decoding via elementary symmetric polynomials; Theorem 2.7: the solving degree of the weight-constraint system S (field equations + ESF equations) is at most 2^r + 1 or 2^r with r = floor(log2 n), i.e. the proven bound depends only on n (not on the code or instance) and is linear in n (2^{floor(log2 n)} ~ n), improving Caminata et al. 2025; Corollary 2.13 gives an instance-dependent variant S' whose bound depends on the rank of a matrix L tied to generalized Hamming weights. PDF intro read.
papers.relevance: Lever 1 methodology: a proven upper bound on the solving degree of a structured Boolean system obtained by analysing S^top (homogeneous top parts) — a template for proving solving-degree bounds for Weil-descended S_{m+1} restricted to subspaces, where the programme has only measurements and closure certificates. Also the ESF Hamming model is the degree-unreduced version of the Hamming-ball membership ideal (KN-OPEN-5e3dd0).
papers.suggested_route: Transfer the proof technique: compute S^top of the Weil-descended S_3 system (binary n=13–21, l-dim subspace) and test whether the Macaulay-matrix argument of Theorem 2.7 yields any nontrivial upper bound; compare with measured d_F. If the top-degree part is a regular sequence (check via Hilbert series with msolve/sympy at toy n) the bound is the Macaulay bound and gives no exponent change — record as accounting.

papers.title: Generalizing Green's Syzygy Theorems to Symmetric Products of Curves
papers.summary: For the n-th symmetric product C_n of a genus-g curve with tautological bundle T_{n,L}: K_{p,q}(C_n, T_{n,B}; T_{n,L}) = 0 when (q-1)deg L + deg B >= (n+1)g + p and deg L >= 2g+1 (Theorem 1); hence T_{n,L} satisfies (N_p) for deg L >= (n+1)g + p (Corollary 2), sharp for elliptic symmetric squares (g=1,n=2: (N_p) iff deg L >= p+3). Proof: weight-one vanishing by induction on n via a filtration of the kernel bundle. Works over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero. PDF intro read.
papers.relevance: Semaev's S_{m+1} is the equation of the locus in Sym^m(E) x E (or the image of Sym^m(E) under the x-coordinate map) cut out by the addition map; the point-decomposition variety is Sym^m(E) intersected with linear conditions (factor base V is F_2-linear in x). Koszul vanishing / (N_p) for Sym^m(E) bounds the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of the homogeneous ideal of Sym^m(E) in the embedding by T_{m,L} (for g=1: quadrics with linear syzygies from deg L >= m+2). This is a geometric regularity statement about the same variety whose Weil-descended equations the programme solves; it is independent of the Galois-group (monodromy) closure, which concerns fibres, not syzygies.
papers.suggested_route: Experiment: embed Sym^2(E) and Sym^3(E) over F_p (p ~ 2^10–2^16) and over F_{2^n} (n=7–13) via T_{m,L} with deg L = m+2, compute the homogeneous ideal and its Betti table / regularity with msolve (Hilbert series) and compare with measured solving degrees of the Weil-descended S_3/S_4 restricted to linear bases; check whether (N_p) persists in positive characteristic for these toy cases (paper assumes char 0). Falsifier: the regularity of Sym^m(E) is O(m) and independent of n while measured solving degree of the descended system grows with n -> the growth comes from the descent/field equations, not from the geometry; then the lever-1 question is about the Weil restriction of a regular ideal, which sharpens where to look. Classification: structural/accounting unless regularity of the restricted system is shown to be bounded in n.

papers.title: Resultant of an equivariant polynomial system with respect to a direct product of r symmetric groups / ... with respect to the reflection group G(r,n)
papers.authors: Sonagnon Julien Owolabi, Ollé Grégroire Kam, Ibrahim Nonkané, Joel Tossa (two companion papers)
papers.summary: Decomposition formulas: the resultant of a homogeneous system equivariant under S_{n_1} x ... x S_{n_r}, or under G(r,n) = (Z/r)^n x| S_n, factors as a product of resultants of smaller partition-indexed subsystems (divided differences indexed by partitions); the discriminant of an invariant polynomial splits accordingly. Abstract only read.
papers.relevance: Lever 3 and the symmetry inventory: S_{m+1} is S_m-equivariant and on 2-torsion curves has the larger D_4 / G(2,n)-type symmetry (the never-run D4-symmetrised S_5 lattice; FGHR symmetric variables). Resultant-based PDP solvers (eliminating variables from the descended system) would get the resultant as a product of much smaller resultants, which is a polynomial-factor saving. G(2,n) is exactly (Z/2)^n x| S_n, the sign-flip plus permutation symmetry of x-coordinates under negation and S_m.
papers.suggested_route: Toy: for prime-field S_4 at m=3 (p ~ 2^16–2^20) with a 2-torsion curve, compute the resultant eliminating one variable both naively (PARI polresultant) and via the partition decomposition; measure degree and time ratio. This is a constant/polynomial factor at best (symmetry cannot change an exponent) — classify as engineering; it may make the unmeasured (m,l) = (4,4),(4,5),(4,6) cells cheaper.

papers.title: A Szemerédi–Trotter Theorem in Arbitrary Fields
papers.summary: m points and n lines in k^2 (char p) determine at most 3(mn)^{2/3} + m + n + 2mn/p incidences (coefficient 1 over F_p), sharp up to constants over prime fields for m=n; polynomial-method proof; consequences: improved sum-product for small sets in positive characteristic, Bourgain two-source extractor error, Furstenberg/projection estimates; formalized in Lean. Abstract read; used by Kopparty et al. above.
papers.relevance: Optimal point-line incidence bounds in F_p^2 are the quantitative tool behind sum-product/additive-energy statements that the programme's x-functional filter question (KN-OPEN-91d4f6) and coordinate-statistic hunts implicitly rely on: a filter defined by linear functionals of (x,y) coordinates evaluated on sums has its single-bucket excess controlled by incidences between the point set {(x(P),y(P))} and lines. Gives an unconditional upper bound on the gain of linear x-functional filters.
papers.suggested_route: Derive: for a factor base F of size B on E/F_p and a linear functional ell, bound #{(P,Q) in F^2 : ell(x(P+Q)) in bucket} using the incidence bound on the chord-and-tangent configuration; compare with the measured collision excess at p ~ 2^20–2^30 (numpy). Expected outcome: gain is O(1) + o(1) — a clean kill of the linear case of KN-OPEN-91d4f6; nonlinear filters remain open.

papers.title: Covering finite fields by translates of multiplicative subgroups
papers.summary: For the index-d subgroup G_d of F_q^* and a covering A + (G_d u {0}) = F_q with |A| = s, proves q <= d^{8s/d} (Bonferroni-polynomial root shifting); covering-probability formula for logarithmic-size shift sets; subfield constructions attain the uniform restriction; characterizes equality in the counting bound by subfield cosets. Abstract read.
papers.relevance: Lever 6 (multiplicative-subgroup base mu_263 in F_{2^131}): how much of F_q is reached by few additive translates of a small multiplicative subgroup is the coverage question for a mu-type factor base (which x-coordinates are sums of base x's is not the same thing, but the additive-combinatorial size bounds are the first-order obstruction). The result quantifies that small subgroups plus few shifts cannot cover F_q unless s/d is large, i.e. a coverage kill criterion for tiny multiplicative bases.
papers.suggested_route: Accounting only: compute for F_{2^131} the implied bound on how many translates of mu_263 u {0} are needed to cover F_q (s >= d log q/(8 log d)) and compare with the base-size/online-cost line B D^2 << N. Expected: a mu_263 base of 263 points is far too small for any m; the bound confirms it with a theorem rather than a census.

papers.title: Recovering curves from isogeny classes of Prym varieties
papers.venue: arXiv math.AG (2609.32065v1); submitted to a volume in honor of Y. Zarhin
papers.summary: Proposes a conjecture that a curve can be recovered from the isogeny classes of its Prym varieties and, motivated by it, analyzes constructions of pairs of curves with isogenous Jacobians and several isogenous Pryms. Abstract page only read (2-sentence abstract, no further detail available without the PDF).
papers.relevance: Lever 10 (Prym / same-field genus-g embeddings, five follow-ups filed 2026-10-27, unexecuted): the constructions of curve pairs with isogenous Jacobians and isogenous Pryms are exactly the raw material for 'E as isogeny factor of a Prym of a same-field cover'. The programme's transport-conservation lemma (homomorphic transfers change decomposition counts by |kernel|^{m-1}) applies to any such isogeny, so the only value is destination geometry/arithmetic.
papers.suggested_route: Read the PDF constructions; for any explicit pair (C, C') with Prym(C'/C) ~ E x A over the same finite field, compute at toy size (PARI point counts) whether the Prym has a cheaper decomposition oracle than E itself (it is a higher-dimensional abelian variety over the same field, so index calculus on it is Gaudry-type with the same field; expected no gain). Falsifier: Prym decomposition cost per relation >= E's at matched base size.

papers.title: Elliptic curves attached to Jacobians with imaginary multiplication
papers.summary: For an odd-dimensional abelian variety A/Q with an imaginary quadratic field M embedded in End^0(A_M) of signature ((g+1)/2,(g-1)/2), there is a CM elliptic curve E/Q with H^1(E) a sub-representation of H^g(A)((g-1)/2). Explicitly: for Jac(y^2 = x h(x^2)) the curve is y^2 = x^3 + h(0) x; for Jac(y^3 = f(x)) (Picard curves) it is y^2 = x^3 + 16 disc(f), via a new p-adic method; application: average polynomial time zeta functions of Picard curves. Abstract read.
papers.relevance: Lever 10 (same-field genus-g embeddings): this is an embedding of H^1(E) into the middle cohomology H^g(A), not into H^1 — so E is not an isogeny factor of A and the relation is a Galois-representation / motivic correspondence, which is the kind of non-homomorphic transfer the conservation lemma does not cover. However E is forced to be CM (j = 1728 or 0), so it cannot be a deployed target; and reductions mod p give E/F_p with H^1(E) inside H^g(A mod p), realized by an algebraic cycle only conjecturally (Tate).
papers.suggested_route: Check whether the sub-representation is induced by an algebraic correspondence that acts on points (if it is, Tate's theorem/transport conservation applies and the lead dies as a relabelling). Toy: for y^2 = x h(x^2) over F_p with g=3, verify the L-polynomial factor of E inside the degree-6 L-polynomial of Jac (PARI), then test whether any explicit map Jac -> E or Sym^k -> E exists via the obvious quotients (the curve y^2 = x h(x^2) has the involution x -> -x, so Jac splits over F_p into Jac(quotient) x Prym; check whether E appears in H^1 of the quotient — if it does, this is just a split Jacobian, already closed).

papers.title: Nakajima-extremal Artin–Schreier covers of ordinary elliptic curves in characteristic 2
papers.date: 2026-09-13 (2 days before window; included as borderline)
papers.summary: Over k = bar F_2, for q = 2^h >= 8 and an ordinary elliptic curve E with invariant differential omega, takes T = E[q](k) (cyclic of order q) and f with simple poles at T and equal residues lambda, and the Artin–Schreier cover X: z^2 + z = f. X is ordinary, bielliptic of genus q+1, Aut(X) = Dih(C_q) x C_2 of order 4(g-1) (Nakajima-extremal, type (ib) of Giulietti–Korchmáros), every type-(ib) curve arises this way, isomorphism classes parametrized by (k^*)^2, a cyclic C_q acts freely with X/C_q ordinary of genus 2; explicit plane model over F_2 for q=8. PDF intro read.
papers.relevance: Cover attacks (GHS) need a curve X -> E with X defined over a small field and E over the big one; here X -> E is a same-field Artin–Schreier cover of degree 2 whose Jacobian contains E (bielliptic) plus a Prym of dimension q, with a free C_q action and a genus-2 quotient. For ECC2K-130 (E ordinary over F_{2^131}) this gives explicit same-field covers with large automorphism groups and small quotients — the structure lever 10 ('Prym / same-field genus-g embeddings') asks for, though the construction needs E[q] rational (q-torsion points are over an extension for a prime-order target, so the cover descends to F_{2^131} only for q=1 or after base change).
papers.suggested_route: Toy: take E/F_{2^n} (n=7–13) with 2^h | #E(F_{2^n}) rational q-torsion, build X(E,omega,lambda,q) via the explicit f, compute the zeta function of X and of X/C_q with PARI point counting over small extensions, and decompose Jac(X) ~ E x Prym; check whether the genus-2 quotient X/C_q carries E as a factor (if so, it is a (2,2)-gluing — LEAD-TRF-second-torsion-direction, closed_obstructed). Name the obstruction expected: transport conservation on the homomorphic part; no intermediate field for prime n.

papers.title: Detecting split surfaces, RM surfaces, and minimum walks on isogeny graphs
papers.summary: Uses refined Humbert invariants to detect (N,N)-splittings of principally polarized superspecial abelian surfaces, and RM embeddings, by primitive-representation problems for quinary quadratic forms, without computing isogenies; experiments up to 1000-bit p show detected splitting degree N ~ p (isogeny degree ~ p^2). Abstract read.
papers.relevance: Lever 10 (Kani/Richelot gluing, 'second N-torsion direction') and LEAD-EXO-split-jacobian-projection (closed_obstructed): detecting at which level a Jacobian splits as E x E' without walking. Superspecial only; ordinary targets not covered.
papers.suggested_route: No experiment proposed: the mechanism (Humbert invariants) is for the superspecial locus; for ordinary E over F_{2^131} the (N,N)-split question is governed by the endomorphism ring Z[tau] of class number 1 (already recorded: nothing at h(O_K)=1).

papers.title: Post-quantum commutative group actions from oriented superspecial abelian varieties
papers.authors: Wouter Castryck, Bogdan Adrian Dina, Péter Kutas, Gioella Lorenzon
papers.summary: Shimura class group actions on CM-oriented superspecial principally polarized abelian varieties; tools: a version of Kani's lemma 'with CM', a dimension-halving trick, representing CM orientations via higher-dimensional isogenies, Ibukiyama–Katsura–Oort correspondence, obstructions to transitivity. Abstract read.
papers.relevance: The only in-window Kani-related arXiv item. Kani-with-CM is a gluing tool for CM-oriented varieties; the target K_0 (End = Z[tau], h=1) is CM-oriented in the ordinary setting, so the lemma formally applies, but gluing is homomorphic and covered by transport conservation.
papers.suggested_route: None beyond noting the tool; LEAD-TRF-second-torsion-direction is closed_obstructed by conservation and the lemma does not change that.

papers.title: The Supersingular Isogeny Problem in Time and Memory p^{1/3+o(1)}, Unconditionally
papers.summary: Las Vegas algorithm for OneEnd / endomorphism ring / isogeny problems for supersingular E/F_{p^2} in p^{1/3} exp(O(sqrt(log p log log p))) without smoothness heuristics: fixes a family of smooth degrees, uses counting of isogenies to Frobenius conjugates and a collision estimate, then splits a degree and matches two lists. Companion: Ouyang–Wei–Xu 2610.21488 (2026-10-15) proves the smoothness-probability bounds making Wesolowski's p^{1/3} unconditional. Abstracts read.
papers.relevance: Query 'isogeny ordinary elliptic curve endomorphism ring' hit; supersingular only. For the programme, endomorphism-ring computation on ordinary curves is polynomial via Z[tau] (Koblitz) and isogeny-class invariance (Tate) closes isogeny walks; nothing transfers.
papers.suggested_route: None; record as not applicable to ordinary targets.

papers.title: Frobenius lifts and point counting for smooth curves
papers.authors: Amnon Besser, Rob de Jeu, Pengju Guan, Muxi Li
papers.summary: Zeta function of a smooth proper curve over F_q from a lift C over a p-adic valuation ring via a globally defined lift of Frobenius acting on H^1_dR, computed through cup products and Poincaré duality; denominator-free if ramification <= p; softly cubic in field degree for smooth plane curves; crystalline Frobenius preserves H^1_dR(C) under the ramification condition. Abstract read.
papers.relevance: Lever 11 (height-compressing global lifts / canonical lifts): explicit, computable lifts of Frobenius to characteristic zero are the machinery for canonical-lift and p-adic-section ideas; the programme closed p-adic jets (GGM-simulable) and CM canonical lift heights (obstructed), so this is tooling only.
papers.suggested_route: None new; could serve as an implementation reference if LEAD-EXO-global-lift-height (open_next_step) is executed on function-field sections.

papers.title: Sharp effective Nullstellensatz for projective Cohen–Macaulay schemes
papers.authors: Zhi Li, Xiankui Meng, Xiaoyu Su, Langfeng Zhu
papers.summary: Sharp effective Nullstellensatz over arbitrary fields for projective Cohen–Macaulay schemes of pure dimension: (sqrt J)^{deg_L X} subset J when J (x) L is globally generated (Ein–Lazarsfeld conjecture), mixed-intersection-number refinements, and sharp radical-power bounds for homogeneous ideals in standard graded CM domains extending Kollár. Abstract read.
papers.relevance: Lever 1 proof route (degree-c pseudo-solutions / closure certificates): Nullstellensatz degree bounds are upper bounds on the degree at which 1 (or a radical power) is reached, i.e. on the last fall degree of an inconsistent or zero-dimensional system. The open question needs lower bounds growing with n; this provides sharp upper bounds in a general setting (and over any field), useful to calibrate what a proved lower bound could at most be.
papers.suggested_route: Accounting: apply the sharp radical-power bound to the Weil-descended S_3 ideal plus field equations (zero-dimensional, degree product bound) at n=13–21 and compare with measured d_F (>= 5 certified at n=33–45): if the bound is far above measurements it says nothing; the value is in the proof technique (Koszul evaluation maps compatible with divisor cuts) as a model for a lower-bound argument. No exponent change.

papers.title: GPU-Accelerated Search for Fast Matrix Multiplication over F_2
papers.authors: Zeke Medley, Anagha Gokul, Quan Luu, Panagiotis Manolios
papers.summary: Flip-graph search for low-rank matrix multiplication schemes on an H200 at >10^9 steps/s up to 7x7; proves the F_2 flip graph is strongly connected with flip and plus edges only; finds 7x7 over F_2 in 245 multiplications (previous 248). Related in-window cs.SC items: 2609.12027 (4x4x4:48 recursive in practice), 2609.18722 (lower bound 21 for 3x3 over F_2), 2609.32388 / 2610.27451 (rank-23 3x3 kernels). Abstract read.
papers.relevance: Lever 13 (hashed-factor-base tensor contraction, conditional on omega <= 9/4 over GF(2^k)): fixed-format schemes do not move the asymptotic exponent; they give constant-factor improvements to the GF(2)-linear-algebra stage (Frobenius-equivariant F4, lever 5).
papers.suggested_route: None for the exponent question; optional engineering: plug a 245-multiplication 7x7 F_2 kernel into the sparse linear algebra path and measure, classify as engineering.

papers.title: Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure (monograph)
papers.summary: Monograph developing finite-field theory via root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality and cyclic modules: linearized polynomials, normal bases and invariant subspaces, cyclotomic cosets as additive stabilizers, 'low-degree representations of subfields with conjugate root blocks', Gaussian periods linked to short linear relations in multiplicative subgroups, Weil bounds for polynomial character sums. Abstract read.
papers.relevance: Lever 6 (non-subspace Frobenius-stable bases at prime n: cyclotomic cosets, trace spectrum, mu_263) is exactly the structural vocabulary of this monograph; in particular 'short linear relations in multiplicative subgroups via Gaussian periods' is the relation-yield question for a multiplicative-subgroup base, and 'root sets' of low-degree polynomials are the membership-degree objects of the 'no low-degree membership' closure.
papers.suggested_route: Use as reference to compute, for F_{2^n} with n prime and a small multiplicative subgroup mu_d, the number of additive relations of length 3–4 among its elements from Gaussian-period identities (PARI, n=11–31, d | 2^n-1 small), and compare with the random expectation d^{m}/2^n; any excess is the 'coverage' lever for a mu-type base. Expected: no excess beyond Frobenius symmetry (accounting).

papers.title: Brauer–Manin obstruction for Weil restrictions
papers.summary: For a quasi-projective variety X over a number field k and its Weil restriction X' to k', the Brauer–Manin sets of X and X' agree (also for Br_1). Abstract read.
papers.relevance: Only in-window 'Weil restriction' hit in math.AG/math.NT; arithmetic over number fields, no algorithmic content for Weil descent over finite fields. Recorded for completeness of the query.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: Brace for impact: ECDLP challenges for quantum cryptanalysis (v3) / Efficient Record-and-Replay Arithmetic for Quantum Elliptic-Curve Point Addition
papers.authors: Pierre-Luc Dallaire-Demers, William Doyle, Timothy Foo (2508.14011v3) ; Jieyi Long et al. (2609.28882v1)
papers.summary: Difficulty-graded secp256k1-style ECDLP challenge ladder (prime field 6–256 bits) with classical rho and Shor resource calibration (v3 refreshed 2026-10-29); and reversible secp256k1 point-addition circuits (Jump-2 / ping-pong record-and-replay GCD) from the ECDSA.Fail effort, 1,419 qubits and ~1.36M Toffolis per windowed addition, with stated correctness caveats. Abstracts read.
papers.relevance: The only in-window arXiv items on ECDLP per se are quantum resource/engineering papers; no classical algorithmic content. LEAD-EXO-quantum-ecdlp-resources is open_next_step in the atlas.
